database_summary: Small mixed dataset combining a pizza/order operational domain (customers, orders, pizzas, toppings, runners, runner trips, recipe components, extras/exclusions) with several unrelated public/demographic data tables (trees inventory, income by zipcode, COVID-like statistics, company funding/dates/industries, a large word list). The pizza portion is transactional/events (orders, runner trips) with reference/dimension tables for pizzas, toppings and runners. Trees and statistics are large observational datasets (measurements/events). Companies tables provide descriptive/company attributes. Schema uses integer surrogate ids and text timestamps; no explicit declared primary keys or foreign key constraints in DDL but natural keys are present (order_id, pizza_id, topping_id, runner_id, company_id, tree_id, zipcode).

accepted.name: pizza_orders_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  co.order_id AS order_id,
  co.customer_id AS customer_id,
  co.pizza_id AS pizza_id,
  co.exclusions AS exclusions,
  co.extras AS extras,
  co.order_time AS order_time
FROM pizza_customer_orders co
UNION ALL
SELECT
  cco.order_id AS order_id,
  cco.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cco.pizza_id AS pizza_id,
  cco.exclusions AS exclusions,
  cco.extras AS extras,
  cco.order_time AS order_time
FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders cco
accepted.description: Normalized base of customer orders combining raw and cleaned order tables. Use when analyzing orders with canonical order_time (as ISO text), keeping both raw and cleaned extras/exclusions and preserving ids for joins. | Use for: count orders by pizza/pizza_name over time; join orders to runner deliveries or extras/exclusions details; filter orders in a time window or by customer

accepted.name: pizza_recipe_topping_map
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pizza_id AS pizza_id,
  TRIM(value) AS topping_id_text,
  CASE WHEN TRIM(value) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST(TRIM(value) AS INTEGER) END AS topping_id
FROM (
  SELECT pizza_id,
    SUBSTR(recipes.toppings, start+1,
      INSTR(recipes.toppings || ',', ',') - start - 1
    ) AS value
  FROM (
    SELECT pizza_id, ',' || COALESCE(toppings, '') || ',' AS toppings
    FROM pizza_recipes
  ) AS recipes,
  (
    SELECT 0 AS start
    UNION ALL SELECT 1
    UNION ALL SELECT 2
    UNION ALL SELECT 3
    UNION ALL SELECT 4
    UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6
    UNION ALL SELECT 7
    UNION ALL SELECT 8
    UNION ALL SELECT 9
    UNION ALL SELECT 10
    UNION ALL SELECT 11
    UNION ALL SELECT 12
    UNION ALL SELECT 13
    UNION ALL SELECT 14
    UNION ALL SELECT 15
    UNION ALL SELECT 16
    UNION ALL SELECT 17
    UNION ALL SELECT 18
    UNION ALL SELECT 19
    UNION ALL SELECT 20
  ) AS starts
)
WHERE topping_id_text IS NOT NULL AND topping_id_text != ''
accepted.description: Explodes pizza_recipes.toppings (comma-separated topping_id list) into one row per pizza_id x topping_id. Use when you need to join recipes to topping metadata or to aggregate toppings usage across pizzas. | Use for: list toppings for a given pizza; count how many pizzas include a given topping; join to pizza_toppings to get topping_name

accepted.name: pizza_orders_with_names
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.order_id AS order_id,
  p.customer_id AS customer_id,
  p.pizza_id AS pizza_id,
  pn.pizza_name AS pizza_name,
  p.exclusions AS exclusions,
  p.extras AS extras,
  p.order_time AS order_time
FROM pizza_orders_base p
LEFT JOIN pizza_names pn
  ON p.pizza_id = pn.pizza_id
accepted.description: Denormalized orders joined to pizza_names to expose pizza_name for each order. Useful for reporting orders by pizza name and downstream grouping or ranking. | Use for: top-ordered pizza names; orders per pizza_name over time; filter orders for a specific pizza_name

accepted.name: runner_trips_clean
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id AS order_id,
  runner_id AS runner_id,
  pickup_time AS pickup_time,
  distance AS distance,
  duration AS duration,
  cancellation AS cancellation
FROM pizza_clean_runner_orders
accepted.description: Canonical numeric runner trips using pizza_clean_runner_orders. Use for analyses that need numeric distance and duration per order/runner and pickup_time. | Use for: average trip distance or duration per runner; join deliveries to orders to analyze delivery times; identify cancelled vs completed deliveries

accepted.name: runner_performance_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  runner_id AS runner_id,
  COUNT(order_id) AS trips_count,
  AVG(duration) AS avg_duration,
  AVG(distance) AS avg_distance,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(duration) ASC) AS duration_rank,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(distance) ASC) AS distance_rank
FROM runner_trips_clean
WHERE cancellation IS NULL OR cancellation = ''
GROUP BY runner_id
accepted.description: Ranks runners by average duration and average distance with counts of trips. Exposes runner-level aggregates plus rank columns for top-K selection downstream. | Use for: who are the fastest runners by avg duration; top-K longest-distance runners; compare runner speed vs trips_count

accepted.name: topping_catalog
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  topping_id AS topping_id,
  topping_name AS topping_name
FROM pizza_toppings
accepted.description: Simple pass-through of pizza_toppings to expose topping_id and topping_name for joins and lookups. | Use for: lookup topping_name by id; join toppings to recipes or extras/exclusions

accepted.name: trees_by_zip
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  zipcode AS zipcode,
  nta_name AS nta_name,
  boroname AS boroname,
  COUNT(*) AS tree_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'Alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS alive_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status != 'Alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS non_alive_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN health = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS health_good_count,
  AVG(tree_dbh) AS avg_tree_dbh
FROM trees
GROUP BY zipcode, nta_name, boroname
accepted.description: Aggregates tree counts and basic health/status breakdowns per zipcode and neighborhood (nta_name). Useful for demographic joins and spatial summaries. | Use for: tree density by zipcode; health status distribution across neighborhoods; join trees to income_trees by zipcode

accepted.name: income_by_zip
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  zipcode AS zipcode,
  Estimate_Total AS Estimate_Total,
  Margin_of_Error_Total AS Margin_of_Error_Total,
  Estimate_Median_income AS Estimate_Median_income,
  Margin_of_Error_Median_income AS Margin_of_Error_Median_income,
  Estimate_Mean_income AS Estimate_Mean_income,
  Margin_of_Error_Mean_income AS Margin_of_Error_Mean_income
FROM income_trees
accepted.description: Pass-through of income_trees table keyed by zipcode to join demographic income estimates to spatial datasets. | Use for: join income estimates to trees or other zipcode data; analyze median income vs tree counts

accepted.name: companies_funding_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  company_id AS company_id,
  valuation AS valuation,
  funding AS funding,
  CASE WHEN funding IS NOT NULL AND valuation IS NOT NULL AND valuation > 0 THEN (CAST(funding AS REAL) / valuation) ELSE NULL END AS funding_to_valuation_ratio
FROM companies_funding
accepted.description: Company-level funding summary exposing valuation and funding amounts with indicators. Use to join to dates/industries and to rank companies by funding or valuation. | Use for: rank companies by funding or valuation; compute funding share relative to valuation; join funding to company founding year or industry

accepted.name: companies_with_dates_industries
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.company_id AS company_id,
  d.date_joined AS date_joined,
  d.year_founded AS year_founded,
  i.industry AS industry
FROM companies_dates d
LEFT JOIN companies_industries i
  ON d.company_id = i.company_id
accepted.description: Denormalized company-level attributes by joining companies_dates and companies_industries. Keeps company_id and exposes year_founded and industry for segmentation. | Use for: filter companies by industry and founding year; join to funding summary to analyze investors by industry

accepted.name: covid_stats_latest_by_state
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  state AS state,
  date AS date,
  total_cases AS total_cases,
  total_deaths AS total_deaths,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY date DESC) AS date_rank
FROM statistics
accepted.description: Selects the latest statistics row per state by date, exposing totals and a date_rank to allow filtering to the most recent period per state. | Use for: get latest totals per state; trend analysis by selecting date_rank <= N; join latest stats to other state-level datasets
